n: Hosea prophesied to the northern kingdom of Israel in the 700s BC, during a time of prosperity under Jeroboam II, followed by chaos and the Assyrian conquest in 722 BC. He was a contemporary of Amos, Isaiah, and Micah.

f.g: Hebrew “salvation”—the same root as Joshua and Jesus.
Jeroboam II, king of Israel about 786–746 BC.

n: God commands Hosea to marry a woman who would prove unfaithful. His painful marriage becomes a living parable of God’s relationship with Israel, who had been unfaithful by worshipping other gods.

f.g: A woman inclined to unfaithfulness; scholars debate whether she was unfaithful before or after the marriage.

f.w: the land hath committed great whoredom
f.g: Idolatry is pictured as adultery against God, Israel’s covenant husband.

n: Hosea obeys and marries Gomer, who bears him a son.

f.g: Nothing else is known of her family.

n: The son is named Jezreel, recalling the valley where King Jehu’s dynasty began with bloodshed. Jehu had been commanded to end Ahab’s house, but his excessive violence brought judgment on his own line—fulfilled when Jeroboam II’s son was assassinated.

f.g: “God sows” (or scatters)—a name with both judgment and hope.

f.w: the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu

n: Israel’s military power (its “bow”) will be broken in the Jezreel Valley, a famous battlefield.

f.w: I will break the bow of Israel

n: Gomer bears a daughter—perhaps not Hosea’s, since the text no longer says “bare him.” She is named Lo-ruhamah, “not pitied” or “not loved,” because God would withdraw His compassion from Israel.
Judah, however, will be shown mercy and saved by the Lord—not by armies. This was fulfilled when God delivered Jerusalem from Assyria in Hezekiah’s day.

f.w: not save them by bow, nor by sword

n: After weaning her daughter (often at two or three years), Gomer has another son.
He is named Lo-ammi, “not my people.” This reverses the covenant promise “I will be your God, and ye shall be my people”—the most painful name of all.

f.w: I will not be your God

n: Yet God immediately promises hope: Israel will become as countless as the sand of the sea, fulfilling the promise to Abraham. Those once called “not my people” will be called “children of the living God.” Paul and Peter apply this to all who come to Christ.

f.w: as the sand of the sea
Ye are the sons of the living God

n: Judah and Israel—divided since Solomon’s death—will be gathered together under one leader. Many see this as the future reunion of all Israel under the Messiah, the latter-day gathering. “Jezreel” now means God will plant His people again.

f.w: gathered together, and appoint themselves one head
great shall be the day of Jezreel
f.g: Jezreel—“God sows”—now points to God replanting His people.
